review_note: Primary-source notes reviewed for this beginner lesson. Notes are paraphrases, not copied articles. The scholarship notice is invented teaching data, never real eligibility advice. No live research occurs during a run.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

notes.text: RAG combines a language model with information retrieved from an external collection.
The original work studied retrieval alongside model training. Using retrieved information at question time does not itself mean retraining the model.

sources.title: Retrieval-augmented generation in Azure AI Search
sources.version: reviewed factual notes 2026-11-13; local note hash recorded by application

notes.text: Retrieval quality matters: search must find material relevant to the user's question, rather than sending an entire collection.
Search indexes can be updated as documents change. Old or poorly retrieved information can weaken an answer.

sources.title: Classic RAG in Azure AI Search
sources.version: reviewed README and indexing description 2026-11-13; local note hash recorded by application

notes.text: A preparation pipeline loads documents, divides them into smaller pieces, and puts them into a searchable index. Some systems also create number-based representations for searching by meaning; these are not required knowledge for a first lesson.
Classic RAG searches first, then passes the search results to a language model to formulate an answer.

sources.title: Retrieve data and generate AI responses with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
sources.version: reviewed factual notes 2026-11-13; local note hash recorded by application

notes.text: External data can help a model answer questions about information outside its general knowledge. Relevant retrieved text can be added to the prompt, meaning the input given to the model.
Citations let a reader return to the original source and check accuracy. Retrieval helps responses but does not promise perfect correctness.

claims.statement: RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation and combines retrieval with text generation.
External material can help answer questions needing facts absent from a model's stored knowledge.
Search for relevant text, add it to the input, then generate an answer using it.
Documents are prepared, split into useful pieces, and organized for search.
Retrieval at question time is distinct from changing model weights through training or fine-tuning.
The relevance of retrieved material affects the quality of the answer.
Documents and searchable indexes need maintenance when facts change.
RAG can still return wrong or unsupported answers; check important claims against sources.
Lesson policy: when the supplied notice lacks an answer, say the information is missing and suggest consulting an appropriate official source; never invent dates or eligibility.
